problem: Existing zero-shot object-goal navigation methods (L3MVN, ESC, VLFM, PSL) lack explicit global layout guidance and so take detours and revisit rooms. Topological methods such as HOV-SG use static waypoints that cannot handle local scene changes.
motivation: Household robots in multi-room homes need globally efficient paths, since the target is often not visible, and must also adapt to local changes such as new obstacles. They should do this without human aid, complex rewards or costly training. The paper therefore combines a coarse global topological plan with a dynamic local planner.
key_idea: Build a dual-level scene memory (a neural implicit vision-language field plus a topometric room/door graph), plan sparse global waypoints on the graph, then densify each segment with an imperative-learning local planner on ego-centric depth, all orchestrated by an LLM agent.
insight: Global topology and local reactive planning are complementary. Without global planning, SR drops sharply as target distance grows (Fig. ablation2). Without local planning (using the robot's point-nav API instead), real-world SR falls from 6/10 to 1/10 at 3 obstacles, versus 1/10 vs 6/10 in the paper's Table. Explore-then-plan mapping cost is amortized over repeated runs: SPL reaches 0.656 after 60 runs, versus 0.389 for ESC.
method: Hierarchical scene representation: a neural implicit function F maps 3D points to CLIP and Sentence-BERT embeddings (Topo-Field style), and a topometric graph G=(V,E) holds region and entrance vertices, both built from posed RGB-D.

Global topology plan: encode the text or image query, compute cosine similarity against embeddings F(P*) at uniformly sampled 3D points to pick p_end, then find the shortest path on G to give sparse waypoints V (doors and corridors).

Local ego-centric plan: project the next global waypoint v_{i+1} into the current depth frame. A CNN depth encoder plus an iPlanner-style imperative-learning planner outputs a dense waypoint set W_{i,i+1}, replanned incrementally as the robot approaches each waypoint.

LLM-powered agent: the context tokens are {background, instruction, hierarchical map in JSON, planning history, trajectory, status, optional skills, action}. The agent chooses among mapping (frontier exploration), planning, and navigation, and handles retries or error reports.
Multi-modal goals: text, image, or 3D position are unified into a destination position. Layout information lets it distinguish instances in different rooms (instance navigation).

setting.backbone: GPT-style LLM agent (frozen) for orchestration; CLIP + Sentence-BERT (frozen); Topo-Field implicit field trained per scene; iPlanner-style local planner (imperative learning)
setting.training_data: Per-scene neural implicit field trained on posed RGB-D from the agent's own exploration; local planner pretrained with imperative learning (no new reward or task-specific training); no extra web data stated
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (480x640, 15 Hz) with odometry pose
setting.action_space: 3D waypoint sets (global sparse plus local dense) executed by a low-level controller
setting.privileged: Posed RGB-D from a pre-exploration pass (explore-then-plan), odometry pose provided; scene map built beforehand

numbers.backbone: LLM agent + CLIP/SBERT + Topo-Field + iPlanner-style planner

numbers_note: Split for MP3D not stated; 'val' used. Metrics printed as fractions and converted to percent. The abstract rounds to 85% SR / 79% SPL. Real-world results are in Table 2 (e.g., chair text 10/10 SR) and are not in the simulator benchmark format.
results: LOG-Nav reaches 85.6% SR and 79.7% SPL on MP3D object navigation, versus the strongest baseline PSL at 42.4/19.2 and HOV-SG at 40.4/23.6. It also does well on instance navigation (text SR 78.6, image SR 67.3). In repeated runs in the same scene, its SPL grows to 0.656 at 60 runs as the mapping cost is amortized.
limitations: Requires a pre-exploration / mapping phase (explore-then-plan); the 1-time-run SPL (0.083) is far below baselines
Local planning does not fully use local scene memory, and detected scene changes are not integrated back into the map or topology
Evaluation on MP3D covers only 6 object categories and compares against baselines that get no pre-built map, so the comparison is not like-for-like
